evidence:
anchor.lisp:46-47 `(sb-bsd-sockets:host-ent-address (sb-bsd-sockets:get-host-by-name host))` has no deadline.
anchor.lisp:65 `(sb-sys:wait-until-fd-usable fd :output timeout)` and anchor.lisp:70 `(sb-sys:wait-until-fd-usable fd :input timeout)` each get the whole timeout.
anchor.lisp:398-401: `(fnn-acquire store)` is followed by load-held and `(fnn-anchor-acquire profile)` while the writer lock is held.
fix: Compute one deadline from TIMEOUT and charge both waits against it. Resolve the name before taking the store lock (or under a bounded resolver), or treat the resolution time as part of the deadline.

reviewer: fnn-anchor-resolve-v4 (anchor.lisp:43-47) calls get-host-by-name with no deadline. The profile host is always a string (fnn-anchor-profile-host, 139-144; int08h is a DNS name), so DNS is always consulted. The two wait-until-fd-usable calls (65, 70) each get the full timeout, so the exchange can take up to 2xTIMEOUT plus resolver time. fnn-command-anchor (around 395-401) acquires the store writer lock before fnn-anchor-acquire and holds it for the whole exchange. This is an operator CLI command, not a served path, so the impact is a stalled command and a held lock rather than a corruption. The ACL2-owned TIMEOUT bound is not what the host enforces end to end.
scenario: With a stalled resolver, `anchor acquire STORE int08h 5` blocks in getaddrinfo for the resolver's own retry schedule (tens of seconds or more), ignoring the ACL2-bounded TIMEOUT (at most 60 s), and holds the exclusive store writer lock the whole time. Even when DNS works, the exchange can take 2 x TIMEOUT. The documented bound (anchor-servers.lisp: TIMEOUT 'admitted only inside this ACL2-owned profile') is not what the host enforces.
title: 'One bounded acquisition' is not bounded: the DNS lookup has no timeout, there are two full-timeout waits, and the store writer lock is held throughout
